# Testament of Dan — 7
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The record of the words of Dan, which he spake to his sons in his last days, in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life. **2** For he called his family together, and said: Hearken to my words, ye sons of Dan; and give heed to the words of your father. **3** I have proved in my heart, and in my whole life, that truth with just dealing is good and well-pleasing to God, and that lying and anger are evil, because they teach men the way of lying and of anger unto blood. **4** And now I confess to you this day, my children, that in my heart I resolved to kill Joseph my brother, and I delighted in the thought that he was sold, because our father loved him more than us. **5** For the spirit of jealousy and vainglory said to me: Thou also art his son. **6** And one of the spirits of Beliar stirred me up, saying: Take this sword, and with it slay Joseph; so shall thy father love thee when he is dead. **7** Now the spirit of anger sought to persuade me to crush Joseph as a leopard crusheth a kid. **8** But the God of my fathers did not suffer him to fall into my hands, so that I found him not when I sought him; and lest I should work iniquity in Israel, he removed him from amongst us.

**2** And now, my children, behold I am dying, and I tell you in truth, that unless ye keep yourselves from the spirit of lying and of anger, and love truth and long-suffering, ye shall perish. **2** For anger is blindness, and suffereth not one to see the face of any man with truth. **3** For though it be a father or a mother, he behaveth towards them as enemies; though it be a brother, he knoweth him not; though it be a prophet of the Lord, he disobeyeth him; though it be a righteous man, he regardeth him not; though it be a friend, he doth not acknowledge him. **4** For the spirit of anger encompasseth him with the net of deceit, and blindeth his eyes, and through lying darkeneth his mind, and giveth him its own peculiar vision. **5** And wherewith doth it encompass his eyes? With hatred of heart, so as to be jealous of his brother.

**3** For anger is an evil thing, my children, for it troubleth even the soul itself. **2** And the body of the angry man it maketh its own, and over his soul it getteth the mastery, and it bestoweth upon the body power that it may work all iniquity. **3** And when the body doeth all these things, the soul justifieth what is done, since it seeth not aright. **4** Therefore he that is wrathful, if he be a mighty man, hath a threefold power in his anger: first by the help of his servants; secondly by his wealth, whereby he persuadeth and overcometh wrongfully; and thirdly having his own natural power. **5** But though the wrathful man be weak, yet hath he a power twofold of that which is by nature; for wrath ever aideth such in lawlessness. **6** This spirit goeth always with lying at the right hand of Satan, that with cruelty and lying his works may be wrought.

**4** Understand therefore the power of wrath, that it is vain. **2** First of all it giveth provocation by word; then by deeds it strengtheneth him who is angry, and with sharp losses disturbeth his mind, and so with great wrath it stirreth up his soul unto destruction. **3** When therefore any one speaketh against you, be not moved to anger. **4** And if any man praiseth you as holy men, be not uplifted: be not moved either to delight or to distress. **5** For first it pleaseth the hearing, and so sharpeneth the mind, and then being enraged he thinketh that he is justly angered. **6** If ye fall into any loss or ruin, my children, be not afflicted; for this very spirit maketh a man desire that which is perishable, in order that he may be enraged through the affliction. **7** For if ye bring against him losses or destruction of that in which he delighteth, he is maddened, and from the madness he begetteth hatred, and from hatred he proceedeth to enmity, from enmity to murder, and murder to death.

**5** Therefore flee the evil imagination also, by seeing beforehand the temptation of Beliar; flee from all lying, and love truth. **2** Keep ye therefore the law of the Lord, and depart from all anger; and love truth and long-suffering. **3** And the things ye have heard from your father, tell also to your children, that the Saviour of the nations may receive you; for he is true and long-suffering, meek and humble, and teacheth by his works the law of God. **4** Depart therefore from all unrighteousness, and cleave to the righteousness of God; and your race shall be saved for ever, and our father shall rejoice over you.

**6** And behold I have told you all things, that I might be acquitted of your sin. **2** For if ye depart from the evil, and cleave to the good, then shall the Lord dwell among you; because he loved Jacob our father and all his seed. **3** But I know that in the last days ye will depart from the Lord, and ye will be provoked to anger against Israel, and will rouse up against her the nations that are hostile to her; for ye will not keep the commandments of the Lord. **4** And ye shall be scattered in all nations, and among the enemies of Israel shall ye be dispersed. **5** But after this, if ye return unto the Lord in truth and with all your heart, he will gather you together out of all the nations, whither the Lord your God shall scatter you; and he will give you into the hand of them that hate you.

**7** And when he had said these things he kissed them, and fell asleep. And they buried him in Hebron.

---
*End of Testament of Dan*
